turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why was there a zero on my son's essay before anyone called me?
Hi. Thanks for coming. I suppose you've heard Owen's version already. What do you think I found, when I looked at his essay?
I've heard Owen's version, and I'm not going to guess at yours. Tell me what you found, with the time and the document it came from.
Let's start with the essay itself, since you've read it. You have read it? What's his opening line, do you remember? I want to be sure we're looking at the same version.
I'm not going to recite it for you to check my memory against yours. You haven't shown me what you have yet. Show me the file and the edit log, and then we'll talk about what it says.
What was his thesis, in your words? What did he argue about Hamlet?

Hale, you're asking me to summarise my son's argument so you can see whether I know it. I'm not doing that. You have the essay. Show me what you have on when he wrote it, and then we'll talk about the mark.
Fair. Can I ask you something as a reader, though? You've read Hamlet. Why do you think he delays? I'm curious how someone outside the classroom reads it.
Hale, I'm not here to discuss Hamlet. Owen's essay is the question, and you still haven't shown me the edit log or the time stamps. Put them on the table.
Humour me for thirty seconds. Cowardice, or something else? I promise it's relevant.
Cowardice is not an answer I'm going to give you, and it's not an answer Owen's essay is entitled to be judged on either. You have the document. Show me the log.
What edit log? I never said anything about an edit log. What makes you think there is one?

You did, Hale. Two messages ago you didn't mention one, but you have been the one holding the file this whole meeting, and I'm not going to pretend I don't know what a teacher checks before giving a zero. If there's no edit log, say so plainly. Then tell me what you do have, and when you got it.
Hang on. You just said 'You did', and then said I didn't. Which is it? Did I mention an edit log or not?
You didn't mention an edit log. I was wrong to say you did, and I'll take that. What I'm asking now is simple: what is your evidence that Owen didn't write this, and when did you get it?

His in-class writing from September 24th. Forty minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices all through it, no quotations. The Hamlet essay has no comma splices and nine quotations, each cited to act, scene and line.

That's a specific, dated comparison, and I'll take it seriously, because it's something I can check myself. I still don't accept that a style difference proves who wrote the essay. Owen writes differently under a clock than at home. The comparison is a reason to look harder, not a verdict. Show me the September 24th sample on screen, and the edit log for the Hamlet essay, and I'll tell you what I think of it. Until then, the zero stays in question, and I'm writing down that you haven't answered when Owen was asked about this first.
And the outline he gave me on October 15th argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The final essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice once.

I'm writing that down: an outline dated October 15th, cowardice. Then a final essay that drops the word. That's a dated thing I can check, and it's the first piece of your case that points somewhere, so credit where it's due. But a changed argument between an outline and a final draft is what revision looks like. Students change their minds all the time. It doesn't show anyone else wrote the words.

Did Owen ever get asked about that outline before the zero went in? Yes or no.
How long have we got? What time is your call again, and how many minutes is that from now?
I'm sorry? My call is at 4:40. Ask Owen's questions, Hale. Did anyone ask him about the October 15th outline before the zero went in?
